title: The Soul's Departure and Prayer
english: The souls of the righteous enter; the gloomy regions of death no longer receive the spirits of the living.
After you, the firstfruits of the living and the dead having become together, so that you may rule over both the dead and the living, all the dead are bold, not by word, the flock.
Do not permit your sparrow to be lured by those hunting or by those meeting at the gates of enemies to plunder my exile from the earth or to disturb my ascent into the heavens.
But this one indeed offered a prayer for himself, while another again offered one for the people of the Jews: “Lord, do not set this sin upon them.”
translator_notes: The text ends abruptly with 'Καὶ' (And), indicating that the text is a fragment.
